feat(mcp): support mainnet in the MCP server, not just Preview

sdk/mcp-server.ts was hardcoded to Preview testnet - network:"Preview"
in every makeLucid call, always reading BLOCKFROST_PREVIEW_KEY, always
loading beni-wallet-state.json (the Preview state file). Any MCP-
connected agent (Claude Desktop, Hermes Agent, etc.) would only ever
be able to spend fake test ADA, undercutting the actual mainnet story.

Added the same BENI_NETWORK pattern used everywhere else in this repo:
set to "Mainnet", it now reads BLOCKFROST_MAINNET_KEY and loads
beni-wallet-state.mainnet.json - the real flagship contract redeployed
earlier this session under the FreezeWallet fix.

Verified against the actual MCP protocol (not a mock): a real client
listing tools, calling get_status (confirms the live mainnet script
address and real caps), and check_limits both within and over the
per-tx cap (confirms the guardrail rejection path with the correct
reason string).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(dashboard): animate the assistant panel closing instead of snapping shut

Closing "Beni" (the chat panel) used to unmount it instantly via a
{showChat && <AssistantPanel/>} conditional - one frame it's there,
the next it's gone. Kept it always mounted and instead animate the
grid column it occupies from 360px to 0px (kept the grid at a
constant 3 tracks so the width itself is animatable - browsers can't
smoothly interpolate a grid losing a track), plus a matching opacity
fade on the panel itself and pointer-events:none while closed so it's
not interactable mid-fade or once collapsed.

Also confirmed, on request: the API and Emergency freeze buttons in
the "persistent header" are intentionally identical across every
dashboard tab (Overview, Approvals, Rules, Whitelist, Transactions,
Monitor) - that header renders once, above the per-page conditional
content, not per-page. No fix needed there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(dashboard): first-visit guided tour

A dismissible spotlight walkthrough (5 steps: workspace, getting
started, balance hero, emergency freeze, ask Beni) shown once per
browser on the dashboard, hand-rolled to match the existing style
(no external tour library - this is a no-build-step CDN React app).

Targets are marked with data-tour="..." on the actual elements;
DashboardTour finds them, measures position via getBoundingClientRect,
and draws a highlighted ring + callout. Skips silently past any step
whose target isn't currently on screen (e.g. the getting-started
checklist, which disappears once a wallet is deployed) instead of
getting stuck. Dismissal (Skip, Got it, or the close button) persists
via localStorage so it only ever shows once.

Verified with a test harness rendering the real Dashboard component:
stepped through all 5 steps confirming correct target + positioning
at each one, confirmed Skip and Got it both dismiss and persist
correctly, no console errors at any point.

feat(cli+docs): simple `flyway` command, easy install, payment option

Two things a first-time visitor needs: a CLI that isn't a mouthful, and
(for Builder Pie) a way to pay.

Simple invocation + easy install
- `pnpm setup` — one command: install, build, and link `flyway` +
  `flyway-mcp` onto PATH (via npm link). After it, `flyway status` works
  from anywhere instead of `node packages/cli/dist/bin/flyway.js status`.
- Root now depends on flyway-cli/flyway-mcp (workspace:*), so without a
  global link you can still run `pnpm flyway <cmd>` / `pnpm flyway-mcp`

- scripts/postbuild.mjs chmods the built bins 0755 so the global link
  survives rebuilds (tsc --build drops the +x bit; root build now runs it).
- README / AGENTS.md / index.html quickstarts use the short `flyway`
  form with a `pnpm`-prefix fallback noted.

fix(npm): sync ~/.devmemory/api_key on install so a stale key can't 401 (0.3.5)

Key resolution reads ~/.devmemory/api_key BEFORE config.json. `install` wrote
the new key only to config.json, so an old/revoked key left in the api_key file
(e.g. from a prior install) shadowed it and every backend call returned
`Invalid or revoked API key`. writeConfig() now also overwrites the plaintext
api_key file whenever a key is provided, keeping both sources consistent.

Bump to 0.3.5. Document the stale-key-file 401 in the main and npm READMEs
(fix: re-install, or `rm ~/.devmemory/api_key`).

docs: cover `command not found` (runner + sudo-prefix) across all surfaces

The npm package README (what npmjs.com shows) was stale — rewrote it with
runner-vs-permanent, start/stop commands, --config-dir, and a Troubleshooting
section. Added the "command not found after a global install" case — npm's
global prefix is often the root-owned /usr/local, so `npm install -g` needs
sudo; a one-time `npm config set prefix ~/.local` fixes it sudo-free — to the
main README troubleshooting, the dashboard Setup page (step 4), and DEPLOY.md.

Setup page now pins `@latest`, so copy-pasting can't reuse a stale npx cache
(the exact trap that made `--config-dir` look unsupported). Also replaced the
now-behind `@0.3.3` example pins with `@latest` (the factual "requires ≥ 0.3.3"
note stays), and added a permanent-command hint to the DEPLOY onboarding.
